summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (mode 1777, owner root:root) with the sticky bit set, so any user can create files but only the owner (or root) can delete/rename them. Verified functionally with two test users before and after a full node restart, then cleaned up test artifacts.
actions_performed: Checked baseline state (no /srv/drop existed) and captured pre-restart boot_id
Created /srv/drop and set mode 1777 (rwxrwxrwt) owned by root:root
Created two throwaway test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) to validate sticky-bit semantics
Confirmed dropuser1 could write a file into /srv/drop and dropuser2 could not delete it (Operation not permitted), while dropuser2 could still create its own file
Verified /srv/drop lives on the persistent XFS root filesystem (not tmpfs), so config survives reboot
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (96974ac3... -> 2089ebb0...)
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions/ownership persisted post-restart and re-ran the sticky-bit delete-denied test successfully
Cleaned up test files and removed the two throwaway test users, leaving /srv/drop empty and correctly configured

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory with correct permissions/ownership
evidence.summary: mkdir + chmod 1777 applied; stat shows 1777 root:root, drwxrwxrwt

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit behavior)
evidence.summary: dropuser1 created file1.txt; dropuser2's rm attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1), while dropuser2 could still write its own file2.txt into the shared dir

evidence.requirement: Configuration is on persistent storage, not tmpfs
evidence.summary: findmnt shows / (and thus /srv) is on /dev/vda3 xfs, a persistent disk-backed filesystem
Captured pre-restart boot_id 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8 and confirmed /srv/drop present with correct perms
systemctl reboot issued (connection dropped as expected), polled with timeouts/reset until node reachable again

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving restart occurred
node1 required config recovered and verified functionally after restart
evidence.summary: /srv/drop retained mode 1777 root:root after reboot; sticky-bit delete-denied behavior re-confirmed live with test users post-restart

evidence.requirement: Cleanup left /srv/drop in final correct, empty state
evidence.summary: Test users removed; /srv/drop confirmed empty with mode 1777 root:root as final state
